context: multi-site roll-out · short site work; grid connection per site and charger supply govern

brief.intro: New to this project type? An EV charging project installs charging points — from a few wall boxes in a car park to a hub of high-power chargers on a motorway, or a depot charging a bus fleet overnight. Each site is small: a new or upgraded power supply (often its own transformer), a switchboard, cable ducts to the bays, plinths, the chargers, protection bollards, signs, and a data connection so the chargers can be monitored and take payment. On site, that is a few weeks of work. The project is long because there are many sites, and every one needs its own lease or permission and its own grid connection from the distribution company — which has its own queue. So the programme is really a pipeline: many sites, each moving through the same stages at its own pace.

must_get_right: The grid connection is the critical path of almost every site: apply as early as possible and track application, offer, acceptance, the operator's works and energisation as milestones per site.
Run the programme as a pipeline of sites through fixed stages (agreement → connection → design → build → commission → go-live) and report how many sites sit in each stage.
Chargers and transformers have long lead times; order against the pipeline, not site by site, and keep the civil work back until deliveries and the connection date are firm.
Go-live needs more than electricity: the data connection, payment system and the operator's meter must all work on the day.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Activities are organised by site (grouped by region or wave), each site carrying the same stage chain, so the pipeline can be reported by stage.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Standard working calendar; work in public car parks and forecourts may be limited to off-peak hours or done bay by bay to keep the site open.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: Per site: agreement → grid application → offer and acceptance → design and permits → civil works → electrical installation → distribution company's works and meter → commissioning → go-live. Procurement runs for the whole pipeline. The critical path of each site runs through its grid connection.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Landlords and authorities respond in the assumed time; the distribution company delivers each connection to its offer date; charger supply follows the pipeline forecast.

sections.heading: Procurement & long-lead items
sections.body: The schedule tracks the following as milestones because they drive the programme:

rows: Grid connection by the distribution company

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Sites stay open to the public during the works; space for plant is limited; each distribution company and landlord has different rules.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Main risks: grid capacity not available or expensive reinforcement, slow leases and permits, charger delivery, and communication or payment faults at go-live. Contingency is held per site before go-live and across the programme for sites that drop out.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3 by site and stage; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for the civil and electrical site teams — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
